qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Direct-to-dealer (D2D) distribution model bypasses independent two-step wholesalers for ~75% of sales, embedding high switching costs via Lennox Premier Dealer certification, proprietary diagnostic tools, warranty handling, and co-op marketing. 10-year median ROIC is ~28% with operating margins near 17-18%. Primary erosion threat is private equity contractor consolidation demanding multi-brand wholesale sourcing.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Lennox achieves high returns on capital via its proprietary direct-to-dealer network, structural runway is limited. Capital Goods base-rate persistence is Tier 3 (10-15Y). The rapid private equity consolidation of independent residential HVAC contractors directly threatens Lennox's captive dealer moat by shifting procurement to multi-brand wholesale distributors (Watsco, Ferguson). Exiting Europe leaves Lennox >90% dependent on mature North American residential replacement cycles, with high-ticket consumer financing vulnerable to structural interest rates.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 28.5% with operating margins of 17-18% and FCF of $640M-$785M. Revenue splits ~65% Home Comfort Solutions (Residential) and ~35% Building Climate Solutions (Commercial); ~75% replacement / 25% new construction. However, Lennox is pure-play North American without global scale, competing against Daikin, Carrier, and Trane. Private equity rollups of local HVAC dealers aggregate buying power away from proprietary direct-to-dealer networks.
